learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Critically and constructively evaluate the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in diverse situations and/or before diverse audiences.
Solve complex problems, autonomously, within the discipline.
Extract conclusions from practical or experimental work and research carried out autonomously.
Effectively apply techniques related to bibliographic search and the use of reliable data sources or other information systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Production and Manufacturing Systems
Fundamentals and technology of forming by material removal
Fundamentals and technology of metal casting and molding
Metal forming processes by casting and molding
Fundamentals and technology of metal forming by deformation
Metal forming processes by plastic deformation
Technology of forming by joining. Electric welding
teaching_methods: Participatory master class, conferences, company visits, attendance at fairs, etc.
Individual or group resolution of cases, role-playing, technique application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.
Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics.
Completion of a project to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities.
Personalized and small group attention. Instruction aimed at reviewing, redirecting class materials, learning, and completing assignments, etc. Specific student inquiries. Scheduled tutorials.
Individual and group preparation of essays, problem solving, projects, etc. For submission and presentation in practical classes.
Student study: preparation of readings, exam preparation, exercise elaboration, class preparation, etc.
assessment_rules: The final grade (N_F) is calculated as: N_F = 0.5·N_PE + 0.25·N_EO + 0.25·N_PI, where N_PE is written tests, N_EO is observation exercises, and N_PI is the integrated project. A minimum score of 4 out of 10 in written tests (N_PE) is required for the grade to be averaged. The course is considered passed if the final grade (N_F) is equal to or greater than 5 points and the written test grade (N_PE) is not less than 4 points. If N_PE is less than 4 points, the course is failed and the final grade will be N_F, capped at a maximum of 4 points. In the second call, only the written test can be retaken, and the grades obtained in other parts will be maintained.
